behavior: Mostly active from dusk through night; stands still or walks slowly in shallow water to grasp prey, roosts socially by day, and nests colonially, though individuals often forage alone.
field_marks: Stocky, thick-necked heron with a hunched posture
Black crown and back on adults
Pale gray wings with whitish underparts
Heavy, pointed black bill and red eyes
Broad, rounded wings, short tail, and long white nape plumes on breeding adults
habitat: Fresh, brackish, and saltwater wetlands, including marshes, swamps, rivers, lake edges, ponds, estuaries, tidal flats, mangroves, canals, and flooded fields, with trees, shrubs, reeds, or other cover for roosting and nesting.
